fyNote: Financial year ends 31 December. 'Net income' is a bank's revenue: interest earned minus interest paid, plus fees and other income.
segmentNote: A regional bank: Malaysia is home, with big operations in Indonesia (CIMB Niaga), Singapore and Thailand (AR p.73).

how.title: How CIMB makes money
how.text: Income = interest earned on loans - interest paid on deposits + fees, trading and Islamic banking income
facts: Income from fees and other non-interest sources

items.label: Depreciation and amortisation
items.tip: Wear and tear on buildings, computers and software.

items.label: Tax and zakat
items.tip: Corporate tax and zakat (Islamic levy) in each country.

items.tip: Profit belonging to minority shareholders in subsidiaries.

Profit to shareholders

pnl.incomeNote: Net income is CIMB's revenue after paying interest on deposits. Plus RM0.42 per RM100 from joint ventures such as Touch 'n Go.

fiveYear.note: Revenue here is net income. Return on equity rose from 7.5% (2021) to 11.3% (2025) (AR p.77).

rows.name: Consumer Banking
rows.tip: Home loans, car loans, credit cards, savings accounts and wealth products for individuals.

rows.name: Wholesale Banking
rows.tip: Loans, bonds, deals advice and treasury for large companies and governments; profit up 17% in 2025.

rows.name: Commercial Banking
rows.tip: Loans and cash management for small and medium businesses; profit down 13%.

rows.name: Digital assets and group funding
rows.tip: Treasury, digital banks (Philippines, Vietnam) and stakes such as Touch 'n Go.

segments.note: Profit is profit before tax. Malaysia earned 61% of group profit before tax (AR p.72-73).

balance.note: A bank's balance sheet is mostly other people's money: customer deposits fund the loans. Shareholders' funds are only about 9% of assets, which is why capital ratios matter.

safety.label: CET1 capital ratio
safety.plain: The bank's own capital as a cushion against losses, as a share of its risk-weighted loans. Management targets at least 14%.

safety.label: Gross impaired loans
safety.plain: Loans in trouble as a share of all loans, down from 2.1% in 2024. Lower is better.

safety.label: Loan loss allowance coverage
safety.plain: Money already set aside covers all of the troubled loans.

safety.label: Loan to deposit ratio
safety.plain: The bank lends out about RM86 of every RM100 deposited; the rest is kept liquid or invested.

safety.label: CASA ratio
safety.plain: Share of deposits in current and savings accounts, which pay little interest and keep funding cheap.

safety.label: Loan loss charge
safety.plain: Yearly cost of bad loans as a share of all loans (0.25% in 2024).

metrics.label: Market value
metrics.plain: What the whole company costs at today's share price: RM76.4 billion.

metrics.label: P/E (FY2025 profit)
metrics.plain: You pay about RM10 for every RM1 of yearly profit. A high number means investors expect growth.

metrics.label: EPS (FY2025)
metrics.plain: Profit earned for each share you own over the year.

metrics.label: Dividend yield (FY2025 dividends)
metrics.plain: For every RM100 of shares, about RM6.7 a year comes back as cash dividends.

metrics.label: Payout ratio FY2025
metrics.plain: Of every RM100 profit, about RM65 is paid out; the rest is kept to grow.

metrics.label: Price to book
metrics.plain: The share price is 1.1 times the accounting value of what shareholders own.

metrics.label: Return on equity FY2025
metrics.plain: For every RM100 shareholders have in the company, it earned about RM11 profit last year.

metrics.label: Net margin FY2025
metrics.plain: What is left as profit for shareholders from every RM100 of revenue: RM34.98.

metrics.label: Revenue growth FY2025
metrics.plain: Revenue compared with the year before.

metrics.label: Profit growth FY2025
metrics.plain: Profit to shareholders compared with the year before.

metrics.label: Net interest margin
metrics.plain: Interest earned on loans minus interest paid on deposits, as a share of lending: about RM2.13 a year on every RM100 lent (2.21% in 2024).

metrics.label: Cost to income
metrics.plain: Of every RM100 of income, about RM47 is spent on staff, branches and IT. Lower is more efficient.

drivers.evidence: Net interest margin fell from 2.21% to 2.13% after rate cuts across its markets, incl. a 25bp OPR cut in Malaysia (AR p.70, p.77)
drivers.why: Lower rates shrink what the bank earns on each ringgit lent.

drivers.evidence: Cost of funds fell 21bps; CASA ratio 42.7% (AR p.70)
drivers.why: Cheap current and savings accounts protect the margin.

drivers.evidence: Non-interest income up 3.1%, now 31.7% of income; wealth AUM +9.2% (AR p.24, p.71)
Gross loans +0.2% (+3.1% in constant currency); deliberately selective lending (AR p.70)
drivers.why: Slow lending limits income growth but protects quality.

drivers.evidence: Gross impaired loans fell from 2.1% to 1.7% (AR p.77)
drivers.why: Fewer bad loans mean lower future losses.

drivers.evidence: Loan loss charge rose from 0.25% to 0.30% (AR p.77)
PBT +17.2% to RM4.51bn on strong treasury and markets (AR p.71)
PBT -13.2% to RM1.79bn from margin pressure and provisions (AR p.72)
CIMB Thai PBT -20.3%; business being recalibrated (AR p.73)
drivers.why: A drag until the restructuring works.

drivers.evidence: Revenue +0.7% reported but +4.2% in constant currency (AR p.73)
drivers.why: A stronger ringgit lowers overseas earnings in ringgit.

drivers.evidence: Up to RM2bn to be returned by end-2027; 7 sen special dividend paid (AR p.71)
drivers.why: Extra cash for shareholders on top of regular dividends.

drivers.evidence: About 9.7 times profit and 1.1 times book value at RM7.08 (see Valuation)
drivers.why: Typical for a large Malaysian bank; re-rating needs higher ROE.

outlook.text: Malaysia's 2026 performance is expected to track the country's positive economic and investment outlook (AR p.72).
Plans to return up to RM2 billion of capital to shareholders by end-2027 (AR p.71).
Keeps CET1 at or above 14% while moving capital to higher-return businesses under Forward30 (AR p.70-71).
External headwinds persist from slower global growth and trade tariffs; Thailand is being restructured (AR p.38, p.73).

outlookOverall.text: Management says Forward30 is progressing steadily, with Malaysia expected to stay strong (AR p.24, p.72).
